_readme: Configurable source list for the web intelligence scan. Edit this file to add, remove or
disable sources -- no application code changes are needed.
FIELDS
name            display name
domain          canonical domain, used for de-duplicating findings across sources
enabled         false = skipped by the scan runner entirely
sourceType      ecosystem-news | global-fintech-news | research-report | accelerator | database
accessMethod    rss | crawler | search | manual  (decides which Apify Actor is used)
feedUrl         RSS/Atom URL when accessMethod = rss
startUrls       entry points when accessMethod = crawler
archiveSearch   { type: "wordpress", endpoint } -- enables per-company historical backfill
(npm run scan:backfill). RSS only serves the newest ~10 posts, so this is
the only way to reach articles older than the current feed window.
priority        1 = highest. Controls scan order and per-run item budget.
scanFrequency   weekly | monthly | quarterly
maxItemsPerRun  hard cap on articles pulled per run, to bound Apify cost
lastScan        ISO timestamp, written back by the scan runner
lastSuccess     ISO timestamp of the last run that returned >0 items
note            why a source is disabled, or any access caveat
ACCESS POLICY
Sources are only enabled where content is publicly available and reachable without
defeating a paywall, login, or robots.txt rule. Paid databases are disabled with a note
naming the licence that would be required -- they are NOT scraped around.

sources.name: TechCabal
sources.note: Open WordPress RSS. Primary source for West/East African fintech funding coverage.

sources.name: Disrupt Africa
sources.note: Open RSS. Strongest single source for African startup funding announcements.

sources.name: Techpoint Africa
sources.note: Open RSS. Nigeria-weighted coverage.

sources.name: Wamda
sources.note: Open RSS. Best coverage of Egypt / MENA-Africa crossover deals.
sources.archiveNote: Not WordPress -- no public archive API found. Feed-only, so history is limited to the RSS window.

sources.name: TechAfrica News
sources.note: Open RSS.
sources.archiveNote: WordPress REST archive returns itsec_rest_api_access_restricted; archive search not attempted.

sources.name: CIO Africa
sources.note: Open RSS. Enterprise-IT weighted; lower fintech-funding yield expected.

sources.name: Business Insider Africa
sources.note: No reliable public feed found; crawled from the markets section. Verify robots.txt on first run.

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.note: Open RSS. High volume and mostly non-African -- relies on downstream relevance filtering.

sources.name: FinTech Futures
sources.note: Open RSS.

sources.name: Fintech Global
sources.note: Open RSS.

sources.name: PYMNTS
sources.note: Open RSS. Payments-heavy, mostly US/EU -- low African yield expected.

sources.name: Africa: The Big Deal
sources.note: Substack RSS covers FREE posts only. The underlying deal database is a paid product and is NOT accessed here -- subscriber-only posts will be truncated by design, which is expected and correct.

sources.name: Africa Private Equity News
sources.note: Partial paywall: headlines and summaries are public, full articles are subscriber-only. Only public content is retained.

archiveSearch.note: Bare host only -- www. returns 404 on wp-json. Archive appears dormant (newest post 2022).

sources.name: Enterprise (EnterpriseAM)
sources.note: Egypt-focused daily brief. Web edition is public; email edition requires signup and is not used. Verify robots.txt on first run.

sources.name: Y Combinator
sources.note: Public company directory. JS-rendered, so needs the browser-based crawler. Used for new-cohort discovery (Phase 4).

sources.name: 500 Global
sources.note: Public portfolio page, JS-rendered. Structure changes periodically -- expect occasional breakage.

sources.name: Plug and Play
sources.note: Newsroom is public; the portfolio explorer is JS-heavy and less reliable.

sources.name: Partech Africa
sources.note: Annual/semi-annual Africa Tech Venture Capital reports, published free as web pages and PDFs. Low frequency; PDF parsing lands in Phase 2.

sources.name: FT Partners
sources.note: DISABLED: research reports are gated behind an email-registration wall. Automating that form would be defeating an access control. Recommended alternative: subscribe to their free research mailing list and drop the PDFs into a watched folder for manual ingest.

sources.name: Crunchbase
sources.note: DISABLED: Crunchbase Terms of Service expressly prohibit scraping, and the data is licensed. Legitimate access requires the paid Crunchbase Basic/Pro API (from ~$49/mo for the API tier). Not purchased -- see the user's instruction. If licensed later, add an apiKey field and switch accessMethod to 'api'.

sources.name: MAGNiTT
sources.note: DISABLED: commercial venture database behind a login/paywall. Requires a paid MAGNiTT subscription or their enterprise API. Not purchased. Their free public blog posts are the only open surface and are low-yield.

sources.name: Briter Bridges
sources.note: DISABLED: Briter Intelligence is a paid licensed database. Public site carries only summary insight posts. Requires a commercial licence for the underlying deal data. Not purchased.
